articles.title: Israel’s Election Deadlock Opens the Door to Another Iran Offensive
articles.description: Israel’s inconclusive election leaves Netanyahu in power as coalition negotiations unfold amid growing indications of possible renewed U.S. military action against Iran.

articles.title: Israel deadlocked / Trump, Iran and the midterms
articles.description: A majority of Israeli voters went against sitting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc, but he may not have to cede his office. It's not clear the opposition will be able to form a governing coaltion.Guest host Scott Detrow talks with NPR International Correspondent Daniel Estrin and NPR National Security Correspondent Greg Myre about how the election could affect Netanyahu's calculus on the war in Iran. U.S. President Donald Trump said that he and Netanyahu "have to finish the job that we started!" And Netanyahu campaigned on a renewed bombing campaign.Email the show at sourcesandmethods@npr.orgSupport public media with NPR+ and enjoy perks for over 25 podcasts like this one.
